\chapter{Pipeline: bootstrap, CI/CD, drift and state}\label{doc-pipeline}}

\hypertarget{1-bootstrap-once-by-an-akeyless-admin}{%
\section{1. Bootstrap (once, by an Akeyless admin)}\label{1-bootstrap-once-by-an-akeyless-admin}}

\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize,breaklines,breakanywhere,frame=leftline,framerule=1.2pt,rulecolor=\color{wo-rule},xleftmargin=6pt]
cd bootstrap
cp bootstrap.tfvars.example bootstrap.tfvars          # platform, repository, gitlab_url...
export AKEYLESS_ACCESS_ID=... AKEYLESS_ACCESS_KEY=... # admin API key (provider env fallback)
terraform init && terraform apply -var-file=bootstrap.tfvars
terraform output pipeline_access_id                    # -> CI variable AKEYLESS_PIPELINE_ACCESS_ID
\end{Verbatim}

Creates:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  OAuth2/JWT auth method \texttt{/governance/auth/ci-terraform} trusting GitHub Actions
  (\texttt{https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com}) or your GitLab (\texttt{\textless{}gitlab\textgreater{}/oauth/discovery/keys}),
  \texttt{force\_sub\_claims\ =\ true}, audience \texttt{akeyless}.
\item
  \texttt{.../terraform-plan} role bound with \texttt{repository} (GitHub) / \texttt{project\_path} (GitLab).
\item
  \texttt{.../terraform-apply} role bound with repository \textbf{and} \texttt{ref=refs/heads/main} (GitHub) or
  \texttt{ref=main} + \texttt{ref\_protected=true} (GitLab).
\end{itemize}

Keep bootstrap state separate and locked down. Delete the admin API key afterwards or keep it as
break-glass in your PAM vault. \textbf{VERIFY:} the plan role\textquotesingle s minimum read rights are not documented;
extend it if a pull-request plan fails with an authorization error.

\hypertarget{2-ci-templates-ci}{%
\section{\texorpdfstring{2. CI templates (\texttt{ci/})}{2. CI templates (ci/)}}\label{2-ci-templates-ci}}

\texttt{ci/github/akeyless-governance.yml} & copy to \texttt{.github/workflows/} in your governance repo \\
\texttt{ci/gitlab/.gitlab-ci.yml} & copy to the repo root (GitLab) \\
\texttt{ci/CODEOWNERS.example} & per-BU ownership of \texttt{model/roles/\textless{}bu\textgreater{}.yaml} \\
\end{longtable}

Jobs: \textbf{checks} (fmt, validate, tests, guard messages, simulator, script tests) -\textgreater{} \textbf{plan} on
pull/merge requests -\textgreater{} \textbf{apply} on the default branch behind a protected environment, followed by
\texttt{akl\_account\_settings.py} -\textgreater{} \textbf{drift} nightly (\texttt{plan\ -detailed-exitcode}, exit 2 = drift -\textgreater{} job fails).

Tokens: GitHub requests an OIDC token (\texttt{id-token:\ write}, audience \texttt{akeyless}); GitLab uses
\texttt{id\_tokens} with \texttt{aud:\ akeyless}. Terraform receives it as \texttt{TF\_VAR\_pipeline\_jwt}; the CLI step
exchanges it for an Akeyless token with \texttt{scripts/akl\_ci\_token.sh} (REST \texttt{POST\ /auth},
\texttt{access-type=jwt}) and passes \texttt{-\/-token}.

Variables: \texttt{AKEYLESS\_PIPELINE\_ACCESS\_ID}, optional \texttt{AKEYLESS\_API}, \texttt{AKEYLESS\_GATEWAY\_API}, and the
JSON maps \texttt{TF\_VAR\_auth\_method\_secrets}, \texttt{TF\_VAR\_event\_forwarder\_secrets}, \texttt{TF\_VAR\_gateway\_secrets}
(secrets/masked). Add your backend configuration.

\hypertarget{3-state}{%
\section{3. State}\label{3-state}}

Remote, encrypted, versioned, access-restricted. It contains API-key access keys, OIDC client
secrets, K8s auth private keys, event-forwarder/webhook secrets, Splunk tokens and the Conjur API
key (provider 2.0.5 has no write-only arguments). Treat the state bucket like a vault.

\hypertarget{4-drift}{%
\section{4. Drift}\label{4-drift}}

Because role rules are authoritative, console edits show up in the nightly plan and are reverted
by the next apply. Tell administrators: "change Akeyless through a merge request; console changes
are temporary". Emergency changes: make them, then raise the MR that codifies them.
